The test `test_indexing_no_materialize` checks whether indexing operations on ExtensionArrays (in this case, a DecimalArray) do not materialize the array unnecessarily. However, the test failed with an exception indicating that it tried to convert a DecimalArray to a numpy array.

Looking at the execution path of the failing test, we can see that the `__getitem__` method of the Series class is called with a boolean indexer (`s > 0.5`). This method attempts to get the value from the index using the `_get_value` method of the Index class.

The `_get_value` method tries to convert the key to a location and then returns the corresponding value from the array. However, in this case, it fails because the `__array__` method of the DecimalArray class raises an exception when trying to convert the DecimalArray to a numpy array.

This suggests that the problem lies in the `__array__` method of the DecimalArray class, which is called when trying to materialize the ExtensionArray. The method is patched with a mock that raises an exception when called, indicating that it is trying to convert the DecimalArray to a numpy array unnecessarily.

Conclusion: The test `test_indexing_no_materialize` checks whether indexing operations do not materialize (convert to a numpy array) the ExtensionArray unnecessary. However, the test failed because the `__array__` method of the DecimalArray class was patched to raise an exception when called, indicating that it is trying to convert the DecimalArray to a numpy array unnecessarily.

pandas.tests.extension.decimal.DecimalArray.__array__
